title: Chemical Bonding II (Geometry) - Chemistry - Molecular Orbital Theory
subject: Chemistry

questions.q: How is Bond Order calculated in Molecular Orbital Theory?
options: (Number of bonding electrons + Number of antibonding electrons) / 2
(Number of bonding electrons - Number of antibonding electrons) / 2
Number of bonding electrons - Number of antibonding electrons
(Number of antibonding electrons - Number of bonding electrons) / 2
questions.explain: The bond order is defined as one-half the net difference between the number of bonding and antibonding electrons. [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-4-molecular-orbital-theory)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why is the oxygen molecule ($O_2$) paramagnetic according to MO Theory?
options: It has an odd number of electrons.
It contains unpaired electrons in the $\pi^*$ (pi antibonding) orbitals.
All its electrons are paired in $\sigma$ bonding orbitals.
It has a bond order of 2.5.
questions.explain: The molecular orbital diagram shows that $O_2$ has two unpaired electrons in the degenerate $\pi^*_{2p}$ orbitals, which explains its paramagnetism. [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-4-molecular-orbital-theory)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Why does the dihelium molecule ($He_2$) not exist in a stable form?
questions.explain: With two electrons in the bonding orbital and two in the antibonding orbital, the bond order is $(2-2)/2 = 0$. A bond order of zero indicates that no bond is formed. [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-4-molecular-orbital-theory)

questions.q: In MO theory, the side-by-side overlap of two $p​$ orbitals results in which type of orbital?
options: Pi ($\pi$) bonding and Pi antibonding ($\pi^*$) orbitals
questions.explain: The side-by-side overlap of two p orbitals gives rise to a pi ($\pi$) bonding molecular orbital and a $\pi^*$ antibonding molecular orbital. [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-4-molecular-orbital-theory)
